options.text: One minus the number of outcomes in $E$
options.why: $P(E')$ is a probability, not a count of outcomes; it equals $1 - P(E)$.

questions.solution_text:
$P(E')$ means the probability of event $E$ not happening.
It is found using $P(E') = 1 - P(E)$.

questions.question_text: William's soccer team wins with probability $0.2$ and loses with probability $0.2$. Every match ends in a win, loss or draw. What is the probability of a draw, as a decimal?

options.why: This is $P(\text{win}) + P(\text{lose})$; the draw probability is $1$ minus this sum.
Subtracted only one of the two given probabilities from $1$ instead of their sum.
